questions.text: Let the domains of the functions $f(x)=\log_4\log_3\log_7\left(8-\log_2(x^2+4x+5)\right)$ and $g(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7x+10}{x-2}\right)$ be $(\alpha, \beta)$ and $[\gamma, \delta]$, respectively. Then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$f$: we need $\log_3\log_7(\cdots)>0$, i.e. $\log_7\left(8-\log_2(x^2+4x+5)\right)>1$, i.e. $\log_2(x^2+4x+5)<1$, i.e. $x^2+4x+3<0$: $x\in(-3, -1)$. So $\alpha=-3$, $\beta=-1$.
$g$: $\dfrac{7x+10}{x-2}\le1\iff\dfrac{6x+12}{x-2}\le0\iff-2\le x<2$; $\dfrac{7x+10}{x-2}\ge-1\iff\dfrac{8x+8}{x-2}\ge0\iff x\le-1$ or $x>2$. So the domain is $[-2, -1]$: $\gamma=-2$, $\delta=-1$.
$9+1+4+1=15$.

questions.text: Let $A=\{-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}$ and R be a relation on A defined by $xRy$ if and only if $2x-y\in\{0, 1\}$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in R. Let m and n be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations, respectively. Then $l+m+n$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$y=2x$ or $y=2x-1$ with $y\in A$: $R=\{(-1,-2), (-1,-3), (0,0), (0,-1), (1,2), (1,1), (2,3)\}$, so $l=7$.
Reflexive: only $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ are present, so $m=5$.
Symmetric: none of the reverses of the 5 non-diagonal pairs is in R, so $n=5$.
$l+m+n=17$.

questions.text: Let the product of $\omega_1=(8+i)\sin\theta+(7+4i)\cos\theta$ and $\omega_2=(1+8i)\sin\theta+(4+7i)\cos\theta$ be $\alpha+i\beta$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Let p and q be the maximum and the minimum values of $\alpha+\beta$ respectively. Then $p+q$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$1+8i=i(8-i)$ and $4+7i=i(7-4i)$, so $\omega_2=i\,\overline{\omega_1}$ and $\omega_1\omega_2=i|\omega_1|^2$: $\alpha=0$, $\beta=|\omega_1|^2$.
$|\omega_1|^2=(8\sin\theta+7\cos\theta)^2+(\sin\theta+4\cos\theta)^2=65+120\sin\theta\cos\theta=65+60\sin2\theta$.
$p=125$, $q=5$, $p+q=130$.

questions.text: Let the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\ 1 & 0 & 1\\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ satisfy $A^n=A^{n-2}+A^2-I$ for $n\ge3$. Then the sum of all the elements of $A^{50}$ is :
questions.sol:
Repeatedly, $A^{50}=A^{48}+(A^2-I)=\cdots=A^2+24(A^2-I)=25A^2-24I$.
$A^2=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{bmatrix}$, whose elements add to 5.
Sum for $A^{50}$: $25\times5-24\times3=53$.

questions.text: The axis of a parabola is the line $y=x$ and its vertex and focus are in the first quadrant at distances $\sqrt2$ and $2\sqrt2$ units from the origin, respectively. If the point $(1, k)$ lies on the parabola, then a possible value of k is :
questions.sol:
Vertex $(1, 1)$, focus $(2, 2)$; the directrix is perpendicular to $y=x$ at the same distance behind the vertex, through $(0, 0)$: $x+y=0$.
Parabola: $(x-2)^2+(y-2)^2=\dfrac{(x+y)^2}{2}$.
At $(1, k)$: $2+2(k-2)^2=(1+k)^2$, i.e. $k^2-10k+9=0$, so $k=1$ or $9$.

questions.text: Let for two distinct values of p the lines $y=x+p$ touch the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{4^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{3^2}=1$ at the points A and B. Let the line $y=x$ intersect E at the points C and D. Then the area of the quadrilateral ABCD is equal to :
questions.sol:
Tangency: $p^2=a^2m^2+b^2=25$, $p=\pm5$; the points of contact $\left(-\dfrac{a^2m}{p}, \dfrac{b^2}{p}\right)$ are $\left(-\dfrac{16}{5}, \dfrac95\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{16}{5}, -\dfrac95\right)$.
$y=x$ meets E at $\pm\left(\dfrac{12}{5}, \dfrac{12}{5}\right)$, so $CD=\dfrac{24\sqrt2}{5}$; A and B lie on opposite sides of CD, each at distance $\dfrac{|-16/5-9/5|}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{5}{\sqrt2}$.
Area $=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{24\sqrt2}{5}\cdot\dfrac{10}{\sqrt2}=24$.

questions.text: The centre of a circle C is at the centre of the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $a>b$. Let C pass through the foci $F_1$ and $F_2$ of E such that the circle C and the ellipse E intersect at four points. Let P be one of these four points. If the area of the triangle $PF_1F_2$ is 30 and the length of the major axis of E is 17, then the distance between the foci of E is :
questions.sol:
$F_1F_2$ is a diameter of C, so $\angle F_1PF_2=90^\circ$.
$PF_1+PF_2=2a=17$ and $\dfrac12PF_1\cdot PF_2=30$, so $PF_1\cdot PF_2=60$.
$F_1F_2^2=PF_1^2+PF_2^2=17^2-120=169$, so $F_1F_2=13$.

questions.text: Let the sum of the focal distances of the point $P(4, 3)$ on the hyperbola $H: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be $8\sqrt{\dfrac53}$. If for H, the length of the latus rectum is $l$ and the product of the focal distances of the point P is m, then $9l^2+6m$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Focal distances of $(x_1, y_1)$ on the right branch are $ex_1\pm a$, so their sum is $2ex_1=8e=8\sqrt{\dfrac53}$: $e^2=\dfrac53$ and $b^2=\dfrac23a^2$.
$\dfrac{16}{a^2}-\dfrac{9}{b^2}=1$ gives $\dfrac{16}{a^2}-\dfrac{27}{2a^2}=1$, so $a^2=\dfrac52$, $b^2=\dfrac53$.
$l=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}$, $l^2=\dfrac{4b^4}{a^2}=\dfrac{40}{9}$; $m=e^2x_1^2-a^2=\dfrac{80}{3}-\dfrac52=\dfrac{145}{6}$.
$9l^2+6m=40+145=185$.

questions.text: The sum of the infinite series $\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac74\right)+\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{19}{4}\right)+\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{39}{4}\right)+\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{67}{4}\right)+\ldots$ is :
questions.sol:
The $r$th term is $\cot^{-1}\dfrac{4r^2+3}{4}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1+\left(r^2-\frac14\right)}=\tan^{-1}\left(r+\dfrac12\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(r-\dfrac12\right)$.
The sum telescopes to $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\tan^{-1}\left(n+\frac12\right)-\tan^{-1}\frac12=\frac\pi2-\tan^{-1}\frac12$.

questions.text: Let the values of p, for which the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x+1}{3}=\dfrac y4=\dfrac z5$ and $\vec r=\left(p\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k\right)+\lambda\left(2\hat i+3\hat j+4\hat k\right)$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}$, be a, b, $(a<b)$. Then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ is :
questions.sol:
$(3, 4, 5)\times(2, 3, 4)=(1, -2, 1)$, of length $\sqrt6$. Joining vector $(p+1, 2, 1)$; dot product $p+1-4+1=p-2$.
$\dfrac{|p-2|}{\sqrt6}=\dfrac1{\sqrt6}$ gives $p=1$ or $3$: $a=1$, $b=3$.
$x^2+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$ has its major axis along the y-axis (semi-axes 3 and 1), so the latus rectum is $\dfrac{2\cdot1^2}{3}=\dfrac23$.

questions.text: Let A be the point of intersection of the lines $L_1: \dfrac{x-7}{1}=\dfrac{y-5}{0}=\dfrac{z-3}{-1}$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-1}{3}=\dfrac{y+3}{4}=\dfrac{z+7}{5}$. Let B and C be the points on the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ respectively such that $AB=AC=\sqrt{15}$. Then the square of the area of the triangle ABC is :
questions.sol:
On $L_2$, $y=5$ needs $s=2$: $(7, 5, 3)$, which is also on $L_1$, so $A=(7, 5, 3)$.
The angle $\theta$ between $(1, 0, -1)$ and $(3, 4, 5)$: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\pm2}{\sqrt2\sqrt{50}}=\pm\dfrac15$, so $\sin^2\theta=\dfrac{24}{25}$.
Area $=\dfrac12\cdot15\sin\theta$, so (area)$^2=\dfrac{225}{4}\cdot\dfrac{24}{25}=54$.

questions.text: Let f be a differentiable function on $\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(2)=1$, $f'(2)=4$. Let $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\left(f(2+x)\right)^{3/x}=e^\alpha$. Then the number of times the curve $y=4x^3-4x^2-4(\alpha-7)x-\alpha$ meets x-axis is :
questions.sol:
The limit is of the form $1^\infty$: $\alpha=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{3\left(f(2+x)-1\right)}{x}=3f'(2)=12$.
$y=4x^3-4x^2-20x-12=4(x+1)^2(x-3)$.
The curve touches the x-axis at $x=-1$ and crosses it at $x=3$: it meets the axis at 2 points.

questions.text: Let $a>0$. If the function $f(x)=6x^3-45ax^2+108a^2x+1$ attains its local maximum and minimum values at the points $x_1$ and $x_2$ respectively such that $x_1x_2=54$, then $a+x_1+x_2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$f'(x)=18(x^2-5ax+6a^2)=18(x-2a)(x-3a)$.
With $a>0$, $f'$ changes from $+$ to $-$ at $2a$ (maximum) and from $-$ to $+$ at $3a$ (minimum): $x_1=2a$, $x_2=3a$.
$6a^2=54$ gives $a=3$, so $a+x_1+x_2=3+6+9=18$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)+2f\left(\dfrac1x\right)=x^2+5$ and $2g(x)-3g\left(\dfrac12\right)=x$, $x>0$. If $\alpha=\displaystyle\int_1^2f(x)\,dx$, and $\beta=\displaystyle\int_1^2g(x)\,dx$, then the value of $9\alpha+\beta$ is :
questions.sol:
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac1x$: $f\left(\dfrac1x\right)+2f(x)=\dfrac1{x^2}+5$. Eliminating, $3f(x)=\dfrac2{x^2}+5-x^2$.
$9\alpha=3\displaystyle\int_1^2\left(\frac2{x^2}+5-x^2\right)dx=3\left(1+5-\frac73\right)=11$.
Putting $x=\dfrac12$: $-g\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac12$, so $g(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}-\dfrac34$ and $\beta=\dfrac34-\dfrac34=0$.
$9\alpha+\beta=11$.

questions.text: A line passing through the point $A(-2, 0)$, touches the parabola $P: y^2=x-2$ at the point B in the first quadrant. The area, of the region bounded by the line AB, parabola P and the x-axis, is :
questions.sol:
The tangent at $(t^2+2, t)$ is $2ty=x-2+t^2$; through $(-2, 0)$: $t^2=4$, and B in the first quadrant gives $t=2$, $B=(6, 2)$.
Area under AB from $x=-2$ to 6 (a triangle) $=\dfrac12\cdot8\cdot2=8$; area under the parabola from $x=2$ to 6 $=\displaystyle\int_2^6\sqrt{x-2}\,dx=\frac{16}{3}$.
Required area $=8-\dfrac{16}{3}=\dfrac83$.

questions.text: If a curve $y=y(x)$ passes through the point $\left(1, \dfrac\pi2\right)$ and satisfies the differential equation $\left(7x^4\cot y-e^x\operatorname{cosec}y\right)\dfrac{dx}{dy}=x^5$, $x\ge1$, then at $x=2$, the value of $\cos y$ is :
questions.sol:
Write it as $x^5\sin y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=7x^4\cos y-e^x$ and put $u=\cos y$: $-x^5\dfrac{du}{dx}=7x^4u-e^x$, i.e. $\dfrac{du}{dx}+\dfrac7xu=\dfrac{e^x}{x^5}$.
Integrating factor $x^7$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(ux^7)=x^2e^x$, so $ux^7=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$.
At $x=1$, $u=\cos\dfrac\pi2=0$: $C=-e$. At $x=2$: $128u=2e^2-e$, so $\cos y=\dfrac{2e^2-e}{128}$.

questions.text: If $\alpha$ is a root of the equation $x^2+x+1=0$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\alpha^k+\frac{1}{\alpha^k}\right)^2=20$, then n is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$\alpha$ is a non-real cube root of unity, so $\alpha^k+\alpha^{-k}=2$ if $3\mid k$ and $-1$ otherwise.
The terms are $1, 1, 4, 1, 1, 4, \ldots$: each block of three adds 6.
$n=9$ gives 18, $n=10$ gives 19, $n=11$ gives 20. So $n=11$.

questions.text: Let m and n, $(m<n)$, be two 2-digit numbers. Then the total numbers of pairs $(m, n)$, such that $\gcd(m, n)=6$, is __________.
questions.sol:
Write $m=6a$, $n=6b$ with $\gcd(a, b)=1$ and $10\le6a<6b\le99$, i.e. $2\le a<b\le16$.
For each $b$, the number of $a$ with $1\le a<b$ coprime to $b$ is $\varphi(b)$; excluding $a=1$ leaves $\varphi(b)-1$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{b=2}^{16}\varphi(b)=79$, so the count is $79-15=64$.

questions.text: A card from a pack of 52 cards is lost. From the remaining 51 cards, n cards are drawn and are found to be spades. If the probability of the lost card to be a spade is $\dfrac{11}{50}$, then n is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
By Bayes' theorem, $P(\text{lost spade}\mid n\text{ spades drawn})=\dfrac{\frac14\binom{12}{n}}{\frac14\binom{12}{n}+\frac34\binom{13}{n}}$.
$\dfrac{\binom{13}{n}}{\binom{12}{n}}=\dfrac{13}{13-n}$, so the probability is $\dfrac{13-n}{52-n}$.
$\dfrac{13-n}{52-n}=\dfrac{11}{50}$ gives $650-50n=572-11n$, so $n=2$.

questions.text: Let the three sides of a triangle ABC be given by the vectors $2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$, $\hat i-3\hat j-5\hat k$ and $3\hat i-4\hat j-4\hat k$. Let G be the centroid of the triangle ABC. Then $6\left(\left|\overrightarrow{AG}\right|^2+\left|\overrightarrow{BG}\right|^2+\left|\overrightarrow{CG}\right|^2\right)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
The side lengths squared are $4+1+1=6$, $1+9+25=35$ and $9+16+16=41$ (and indeed the first two vectors add to the third).
For any triangle, $AG^2+BG^2+CG^2=\dfrac13\left(a^2+b^2+c^2\right)=\dfrac{82}{3}$.
$6\times\dfrac{82}{3}=164$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int\frac{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^{10}}{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)^9}\,dx=\frac1m\left(\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^n\left(n\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)\right)+C$ where C is the constant of integration and $m, n\in\mathbf{N}$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Put $t=\sqrt{1+x^2}+x$; then $\sqrt{1+x^2}-x=\dfrac1t$, $x=\dfrac12\left(t-\dfrac1t\right)$, $dx=\dfrac12\left(1+\dfrac1{t^2}\right)dt$.
Integral $=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int(t^{19}+t^{17})\,dt=\frac{t^{20}}{40}+\frac{t^{18}}{36}+C$.
Since $\sqrt{1+x^2}=\dfrac12\left(t+\dfrac1t\right)$: $t^{19}\left(19\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)=9t^{20}+10t^{18}$, and $\dfrac{9t^{20}+10t^{18}}{360}=\dfrac{t^{20}}{40}+\dfrac{t^{18}}{36}$.
So $n=19$, $m=360$ and $m+n=379$.

questions.text: For the determination of refractive index of glass slab, a travelling microscope is used whose main scale contains 300 equal divisions equals to 15 cm. The vernier scale attached to the microscope has 25 divisions equals to 24 divisions of main scale. The least count (LC) of the travelling microscope is (in cm) :
questions.sol:
1 MSD $=\dfrac{15}{300}=0.05$ cm; 25 VSD $=24$ MSD, so 1 VSD $=\dfrac{24}{25}$ MSD.
LC $=1$ MSD $-$ 1 VSD $=\dfrac{1}{25}\times0.05=0.002$ cm.

questions.text: In an electromagnetic system, a quantity defined as the ratio of electric dipole moment and magnetic dipole moment has dimension of $[M^PL^QT^RA^S]$. The value of P and Q are :
questions.sol:

questions.text: A wheel is rolling on a plane surface. The speed of a particle on the highest point of the rim is 8 m/s. The speed of the particle on the rim of the wheel at the same level as the centre of wheel, will be :
questions.sol:
In rolling without slipping the top point moves at $2v$, so $v=4$ m/s for the centre.
A rim point level with the centre has velocity $v$ (forward) plus $v$ (vertical, from rotation), at right angles.
Speed $=\sqrt2\,v=4\sqrt2$ m/s.

questions.text:
An object is kept at rest at a distance of 3R above the earth's surface where R is earth's radius. The minimum speed with which it must be projected so that it does not return to earth is :
(Assume M = mass of earth, G = Universal gravitational constant)
questions.sol:
The object is at $r=R+3R=4R$ from the centre.
To escape, $\dfrac12mv^2=\dfrac{GMm}{4R}$, so $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{2R}}$.

questions.text:
The displacement $x$ versus time graph is shown below.
(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is 10 m/s
(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is 0 m/s
(C) The instantaneous velocity at t = 2 s is 5 m/s
(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at t = 6.5 s are equal
(E) The average velocity from t = 0 to t = 9 s is zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
From the graph: $x(0)=0$, $x(1)=-5$, $x(2)=0$, $x(3)=5$, $x(5)=5$, $x(6)=10$, $x(7)=0$, $x(8)=-5$, $x(9)=0$ m.
(A) $\dfrac{5-0}{3}=\dfrac53$ m/s: false. (B) $\dfrac{5-5}{2}=0$: true. (C) slope of AC $=\dfrac{5-(-5)}{3-1}=5$ m/s: true.
(D) average from 5 to 7 s $=\dfrac{0-5}{2}=-2.5$ m/s, but the slope of EF at 6.5 s is $-10$ m/s: false. (E) $x(9)=x(0)$: true.
Answer: (B), (C), (E).

questions.text: Consider a rectangular sheet of solid material of length $l=9$ cm and width $d=4$ cm. The coefficient of linear expansion is $\alpha=3.1\times10^{-5}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature and one atmospheric pressure. The mass of sheet $m=0.1$ kg and the specific heat capacity $C_v=900$ J kg$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$. If the amount of heat supplied to the material is $8.1\times10^2$ J then change in area of the rectangular sheet is :
questions.sol:
$\Delta T=\dfrac{Q}{mC}=\dfrac{810}{0.1\times900}=9$ K.
$\Delta A=2\alpha A\Delta T=2\times3.1\times10^{-5}\times(36\times10^{-4})\times9\approx2.0\times10^{-6}$ m$^2$.

questions.text: A cylindrical rod of length 1 m and radius 4 cm is mounted vertically. It is subjected to a shear force of $10^5$ N at the top. Considering infinitesimally small displacement in the upper edge, the angular displacement $\theta$ of the rod axis from its original position would be : (shear moduli, $G=10^{10}$ N/m$^2$ )
questions.sol:
Shear stress $=\dfrac{F}{\pi r^2}=\dfrac{10^5}{\pi\times16\times10^{-4}}=\dfrac{6.25\times10^7}{\pi}$ N/m$^2$.
$\theta=\dfrac{\text{stress}}{G}=\dfrac{6.25\times10^{-3}}{\pi}=\dfrac{1}{160\pi}$.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Isobaric(I) $\Delta Q=\Delta W$
(B) Isochoric(II) $\Delta Q=\Delta U$
(C) Adiabatic(III) $\Delta Q=$ zero
(D) Isothermal(IV) $\Delta Q=\Delta U+P\Delta V$
$\Delta Q=$ Heat supplied
$\Delta W=$ Work done by the system
$\Delta U=$ Change in internal energy
P = Pressure of the system
$\Delta V=$ Change in volume of the system
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Isobaric: $W=P\Delta V$, so $\Delta Q=\Delta U+P\Delta V$ (IV). Isochoric: $W=0$, so $\Delta Q=\Delta U$ (II).
Adiabatic: $\Delta Q=0$ (III). Isothermal (ideal gas): $\Delta U=0$, so $\Delta Q=\Delta W$ (I).

questions.text: Three parallel plate capacitors $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ each of capacitance 5 $\mu$F are connected as shown in figure. The effective capacitance between points A and B, when the space between the parallel plates of $C_1$ capacitor is filled with a dielectric medium having dielectric constant of 4, is :

With the dielectric, $C_1=4\times5=20$ $\mu$F.

questions.text: There are 'n' number of identical electric bulbs, each is designed to draw a power p independently from the mains supply. They are now joined in series across the mains supply. The total power drawn by the combination is :
questions.sol:
Each bulb has resistance $R=\dfrac{V^2}{p}$.
In series the total resistance is $nR$, so the power drawn is $\dfrac{V^2}{nR}=\dfrac pn$.

questions.text: From the combination of resistors with resistances values $R_1=R_2=R_3=5\ \Omega$ and $R_4=10\ \Omega$, which of the following combination is the best circuit to get an equivalent resistance of $6\Omega$ ?
questions.sol:
Circuit (3): $R_1+R_2=10\ \Omega$ in parallel with $R_3+R_4=15\ \Omega$ gives $\dfrac{10\times15}{25}=6\ \Omega$.
For comparison, circuit (2) gives $\dfrac{20\times5}{25}=4\ \Omega$ and circuit (4) (all in parallel) gives $\dfrac{10}{7}\ \Omega$.

questions.text: A metallic ring is uniformly charged as shown in figure. AC and BD are two mutually perpendicular diameters. Electric field due to arc AB at 'O' is 'E' in magnitude. What would be the magnitude of electric field at 'O' due to arc ABC ?
questions.sol:
The field of a uniformly charged quarter arc at the centre has magnitude E along the bisector of the arc.
Arc ABC is two quarter arcs, AB and BC, whose bisectors are at $90^\circ$ to each other.
Resultant $=\sqrt{E^2+E^2}=\sqrt2E$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A finite size object is placed normal to the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. A plane mirror is now placed in such a way that the image produced by both the mirrors coincide with each other. The distance between the two mirrors is :
questions.sol:
Convex mirror: $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1f-\dfrac1u=\dfrac1{30}+\dfrac1{30}$, so $v=15$ cm behind it; the image is $30+15=45$ cm from the object.
A plane mirror at distance $x$ from the object forms its image $2x$ from the object, so $x=22.5$ cm.
The plane mirror is $30-22.5=7.5$ cm in front of the convex mirror.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two polarisers $P_1$ and $P_2$ are placed in such a way that the intensity of the transmitted light will be zero. A third polariser $P_3$ is inserted in between $P_1$ and $P_2$, at particular angle between $P_2$ and $P_3$. The transmitted intensity of the light passing the through all three polarisers is maximum. The angle between the polarisers $P_2$ and $P_3$ is :
questions.sol:
$P_1$ and $P_2$ are crossed. If $P_3$ makes angle $\theta$ with $P_2$, it makes $\dfrac\pi2-\theta$ with $P_1$.
$I=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^2\left(\dfrac\pi2-\theta\right)\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{I_0}{8}\sin^22\theta$, greatest at $\theta=\dfrac\pi4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The dimensions of Planck's constant and angular momentum are same.
Statement (II) : In Bohr's model electron revolve around the nucleus only in those orbits for which angular momentum is integral multiple of Planck's constant.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
$h$ has unit J s $=$ kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, the same as angular momentum: Statement I is correct.
Bohr's condition is $L=n\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$, an integral multiple of $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$, not of $h$: Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A radioactive material P first decays into Q and then Q decays to non-radioactive material R. Which of the following figure represents time dependent mass of P, Q and R ?
questions.sol:
P decays exponentially from its initial value.
Q starts at zero, rises while it is being formed faster than it decays, reaches a maximum and then falls to zero.
R (stable) starts at zero and keeps increasing towards the initial mass of P.
Graph (1) shows this.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider a n-type semiconductor in which $n_e$ and $n_h$ are number of electrons and holes, respectively.
(A) Holes are minority carriers
(B) The dopant is a pentavalent atom
(C) $n_en_h\ne n_i^2$
(where $n_i$ is number of electrons or holes in semiconductor when it is intrinsic form)
(D) $n_en_h\ge n_i^2$
(E) The holes are not generated due to the donors
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
In an n-type semiconductor the dopant is pentavalent (B) and electrons are the majority carriers, holes the minority (A).
The donors supply electrons only; holes come from thermal generation (E).
In equilibrium $n_en_h=n_i^2$, so (C) is wrong.
Answer: (A), (B), (E).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A block of mass 25 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface by a force at an angle $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. The friction coefficient between the block and the surface is 0.25. The block travels at a uniform velocity. The workdone by the applied force during a displacement of 5 m of the block is :
questions.sol:
Uniform velocity: $F\cos45^\circ=\mu(mg-F\sin45^\circ)$, so $\dfrac{F}{\sqrt2}(1+\mu)=\mu mg$ and $\dfrac{F}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{0.25\times25\times9.8}{1.25}=49$ N.
$W=F\cos45^\circ\times5=49\times5=245$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: There are two vessels filled with an ideal gas where volume of one is double the volume of other. The large vessel contains the gas at 8 kPa at 1000 K while the smaller vessel contains the gas at 7 kPa at 500 K. If the vessels are connected to each other by a thin tube allowing the gas to flow and the temperature of both vessels is maintained at 600 K, at steady state the pressure in the vessels will be (in kPa).
questions.sol:
The total number of moles is conserved: $\dfrac{8(2V)}{1000}+\dfrac{7V}{500}=\dfrac{P(3V)}{600}$ (common factor $R$ cancelled).
$0.016+0.014=\dfrac{P}{200}$, so $P=6$ kPa.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, two slits are located 1.5 mm apart. The distance of screen from slits is 2 m and the wavelength of the source is 400 nm. If the 20 maxima of the double slit pattern are contained within the central maximum of the single slit diffraction pattern, then the width of each slit is $x\times10^{-3}$ cm, where x-value is ______.
questions.sol:
Fringe width $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$; width of the central diffraction maximum $=\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}$.
$20\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}=\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}$ gives $a=\dfrac{d}{10}=0.15$ mm $=15\times10^{-3}$ cm.
$x=15$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
If an optical medium possesses a relative permeability of $\dfrac{10}{\pi}$ and relative permittivity of $\dfrac{1}{0.0885}$, then the velocity of light is greater in vacuum than that in this medium by __________ times.
$(\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ H/m, $\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ F/m, $c=3\times10^8$ m/s$)$
questions.sol: $\dfrac{c}{v}=\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}=\sqrt{\dfrac{10}{\pi}\times\dfrac{1}{0.0885}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{10}{0.278}}\approx\sqrt{36}=6$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An inductor of self inductance 1 H is connected in series with a resistor of $100\pi$ ohm and an ac supply of $100\pi$ volt, 50 Hz. Maximum current flowing in the circuit is __________ A.
questions.sol:
$X_L=2\pi fL=100\pi\ \Omega$, so $Z=\sqrt{(100\pi)^2+(100\pi)^2}=100\sqrt2\,\pi\ \Omega$.
$I_{rms}=\dfrac{100\pi}{100\sqrt2\,\pi}=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$ A (taking $100\pi$ V as the rms value).
$I_{max}=\sqrt2\,I_{rms}=1$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle of charge 1.6 $\mu$C and mass 16 $\mu$g is present in a strong magnetic field of 6.28 T. The particle is then fired perpendicular to magnetic field. The time required for the particle to return to original location for the first time is __________ s. $(\pi=3.14)$
questions.note: The time period works out to 0.01 s. NTA's final key gives 0, i.e. 0.01 rounded to the nearest integer (the numerical answers in this paper are integers), so 0 is the answer marked correct here.
questions.sol:
The particle moves on a circle and first returns after one period: $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}=\dfrac{6.28\times16\times10^{-9}}{1.6\times10^{-6}\times6.28}=0.01$ s.
Rounded to the nearest integer (as in NTA's key): 0.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A solid sphere with uniform density and radius R is rotating initially with constant angular velocity $(\omega_1)$ about its diameter. After some time during the rotation its starts loosing mass at a uniform rate, with no change in its shape. The angular velocity of the sphere when its radius become R/2 is $x\omega_1$. The value of x is ______.
questions.note: The key's 32 assumes the angular momentum of the shrinking sphere stays constant. Strictly, if the lost mass leaves without any torque on the rest (carrying its own angular momentum away), the angular velocity would not change. The key is followed here.
questions.sol:
Treating the angular momentum $I\omega$ as unchanged (as intended): $I=\dfrac25MR^2$, and with uniform density $M\propto R^3$, so $I\propto R^5$.
At radius $\dfrac R2$, $I$ falls to $\dfrac{I}{32}$, so $\omega=32\omega_1$.
$x=32$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
Consider the given data :
(a) $\mathrm{HCl(g)+10\,H_2O(l)\rightarrow HCl.10\,H_2O}$ $\Delta H=-69.01$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
(b) $\mathrm{HCl(g)+40\,H_2O(l)\rightarrow HCl.40\,H_2O}$ $\Delta H=-72.79$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Choose the correct statement :
options: The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent.
The heat of dilution for the HCl ($\mathrm{HCl.10\,H_2O}$ to $\mathrm{HCl.40\,H_2O}$) is 3.78 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Dissolution of gas in water is an endothermic process.
The heat of formation of HCl solution is represented by both (a) and (b).
questions.sol:
The two enthalpies differ only in the amount of water, so the heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent: (1) is correct.
Heat of dilution $=-72.79-(-69.01)=-3.78$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (heat is released), not $+3.78$: (2) is wrong. Both values are negative, so dissolution is exothermic: (3) is wrong. (a) and (b) are enthalpies of solution, not of formation: (4) is wrong.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Molal depression constant $K_f$ is given by $\dfrac{M_1RT_f}{\Delta S_{fus}}$, where symbols have their usual meaning.
Statement (II) : $K_f$ for benzene is less than the $K_f$ for water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
$K_f=\dfrac{M_1RT_f^2}{\Delta_{fus}H}$ and $\Delta S_{fus}=\dfrac{\Delta_{fus}H}{T_f}$, so $K_f=\dfrac{M_1RT_f}{\Delta S_{fus}}$: Statement I is correct.
$K_f$(benzene) $=5.12$ K kg mol$^{-1}$, larger than $K_f$(water) $=1.86$ K kg mol$^{-1}$: Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text: Half life of zero order reaction A $\rightarrow$ product is 1 hour, when initial concentration of reactant is 2.0 mol L$^{-1}$. The time required to decrease concentration of A from 0.50 to 0.25 mol L$^{-1}$ is :

questions.text: Consider the following plots of log of rate constant k (log k) vs $\dfrac1T$ for three different reactions. The correct order of activation energies of these reactions is :
questions.sol:
$\log k=\log A-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303RT}$: the slope of $\log k$ against $\dfrac1T$ is $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303R}$, so a steeper line means a larger $E_a$.
Line 2 is steepest, then line 1, and line 3 is the flattest.
$E_{a2}>E_{a1}>E_{a3}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : For $\mathrm{\ddot{C}lF_3}$, all three possible structures may be drawn as follows.
Statement (II) : Structure III is most stable, as the orbitals having the lone pairs are axial, where the lp $-$ bp repulsion is minimum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Cl in $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement; the three drawings I, II and III are the possible placements: Statement I is correct.
The most stable structure is I, with both lone pairs equatorial (fewest $90^\circ$ lone pair interactions), giving the T shape. Lone pairs are not placed axially: Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text: The elements of Group 13 with highest and lowest first ionisation enthalpies are respectively :
questions.sol:
First ionisation enthalpies (kJ mol$^{-1}$): B 801, Al 577, Ga 579, In 558, Tl 589.
Highest: B; lowest: In.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The first ionisation enthalpy of group 14 elements is higher than the corresponding elements of group 13.
Statement (II) : Melting points and boiling points of group 13 elements are in general much higher than those of corresponding elements of group 14.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Across a period the nuclear charge increases and the size decreases, so each group 14 element has a higher first ionisation enthalpy than its group 13 neighbour (B 801 < C 1086, Al 577 < Si 786, and so on): Statement I is correct.
Group 14 elements (C, Si, Ge with giant covalent structures) have generally higher melting and boiling points than group 13 elements: Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: 'X' is the number of electrons in $t_{2g}$ orbitals of the most stable complex ion among $\mathrm{[Fe(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{[FeCl_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$. The nature of oxide of vanadium of the type $\mathrm{V_2O_X}$ is :
questions.note: The most stable ion is the chelate $\mathrm{[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$ ($\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $d^5$). Taking oxalate as a weak-field ligand gives $t_{2g}^3e_g^2$, X $=3$ and $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$, which is basic (option 3). NTA's final key gives "Amphoteric", which corresponds to X $=5$ (low-spin $t_{2g}^5$, $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$, amphoteric). The key is followed here.
questions.sol:
Among the four, the chelate $\mathrm{[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$ is the most stable (chelate effect); it contains $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $3d^5$.
NTA's key treats it as $t_{2g}^5$, so X $=5$ and the oxide is $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$, which is amphoteric (it dissolves in both acids and alkalis).
(With oxalate taken as weak field, $t_{2g}^3e_g^2$, X would be 3 and $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$ is basic.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$ and $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ complex species based on the number of unpaired electrons present is :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ $d^5$ high spin, 5 unpaired. $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ $d^6$ high spin, 4.
$\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$: $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ $d^8$ square planar, 0. $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$: Ni(0) $d^{10}$, 0.
Order: $5>4>0=0$, option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The incorrect relationship in the following pairs in relation to ionisation enthalpies is :
questions.sol:
The ionisation enthalpy of an ion is the energy to remove its next electron.
$\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ ($3d^5$, half-filled) is harder to ionise than $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($3d^6$, which becomes $3d^5$ on ionisation): third ionisation enthalpies are Mn 3248 and Fe 2957 kJ mol$^{-1}$. So "$\mathrm{Mn^{2+}<Fe^{2+}}$" is incorrect.
The others hold: $\mathrm{Mn^+}$ ($3d^54s^1$) 1509 < $\mathrm{Cr^+}$ ($3d^5$) 1592; and a higher charge on the same element always needs more energy.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
(Separation of)		List - II
(Separation Technique)
(A) Aniline from aniline-water mixture(I) Simple distillation
(B) Glycerol from spent-lye in soap industry(II) Fractional distillation
(C) Different fractions of crude oil in petroleum industry(III) Distillation at reduced pressure
(D) Chloroform-Aniline mixture(IV) Steam distillation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Aniline is steam volatile and immiscible with water: steam distillation (IV).
(B) Glycerol decomposes near its boiling point: distillation under reduced pressure (III).
(C) Crude oil fractions have close boiling points: fractional distillation (II).
(D) Chloroform (b.p. 334 K) and aniline (b.p. 457 K) differ widely: simple distillation (I).

questions.text: In which pairs, the first ion is more stable than the second ?
questions.sol:
(A) The OMe group stabilises the adjacent carbocation by $+R$ (lone pair donation), more than Me does by hyperconjugation: first more stable.
(B) The o-nitrophenyl group stabilises a carbanion ($-R$, $-I$) but destabilises a carbocation: first more stable.
(C) The second cation is allylic (resonance stabilised), the first is primary: second more stable.
(D) The OMe-substituted cation is resonance stabilised, more than tert-butyl: second more stable.
Answer: (A) & (B).

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the following compound is :
questions.sol:
The chain of 7 carbons contains C=C, C$\equiv$C and OH; the OH is the principal group and is named as the suffix "-ol" (not as a "hydroxy" prefix).
Numbering from either end puts the multiple bonds at 1 and 6 and OH at 4; when there is a choice, the double bond gets the lower number.
Name: hept-1-en-6-yn-4-ol.

questions.text:
Consider the following molecule (X).
The structure of X is
The major product formed when the given molecule (X) is treated with HBr (1 eq) is :
questions.sol:
X has two disubstituted ring C=C bonds and one trisubstituted C=C (in the lower five-membered ring, at a ring-fusion carbon).
HBr adds by electrophilic addition: protonation of the trisubstituted alkene gives a tertiary carbocation at the ring-fusion carbon, the most stable cation available.
Bromide adds there (Markovnikov), giving the tertiary bromide of option (1); the other two C=C bonds are untouched.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Alcohols are formed when alkyl chlorides are treated with aqueous potassium hydroxide by elimination reaction.
Statement (II) : In alcoholic potassium hydroxide, alkyl chlorides form alkenes by abstracting the hydrogen from the $\beta$-carbon.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
With aqueous KOH, $\mathrm{OH^-}$ replaces Cl by nucleophilic substitution, not elimination: Statement I is incorrect.
Alcoholic KOH (alkoxide) acts as a base, removing a $\beta$-hydrogen to give an alkene ($\beta$-elimination): Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which among the following compounds give yellow solid when reacted with NaOI/NaOH ?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
The yellow solid is iodoform, $\mathrm{CHI_3}$. It forms from methyl ketones $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ and from alcohols $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$ (oxidised to methyl ketones), but not from carboxylic acids.
(A) butan-2-ol: yes. (B) propan-1-ol: no. (C) butan-2-one: yes. (D) ethanoic acid: no. (E) propanal: no.
Answer: (A) and (C).

questions.text: A toxic compound "A" when reacted with NaCN in aqueous acidic medium yields an edible cooking component and food preservative "B". "B" is converted to "C" by diborane and can be used as an additive to petrol to reduce emission. "C" upon reaction with oleum at 140$^\circ$C yields an inhalable anesthetic "D". Identify "A", "B", "C" & "D", respectively :
options: Acetaldehyde; 2-hydroxypropanoic acid; propanoic acid; dipropyl ether
Methanol; acetic acid; ethanol; diethyl ether
questions.sol:
B is the cooking ingredient and preservative acetic acid (vinegar); diborane reduces it to ethanol (C), which is blended with petrol.
Ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 K gives diethyl ether (D), an old inhalation anaesthetic.
A, the toxic starting material, is methanol. Option (4).

questions.text: The correct order of basicity for the following molecules is :
questions.sol:
In R (a bridged bicyclic lactam) the nitrogen lone pair cannot line up with the C=O $\pi$ system (Bredt's rule), so it is not delocalised and R is by far the most basic.
In Q the C=C conjugated with the C=O already supplies electron density to the carbonyl, so the carbonyl draws less on the nitrogen lone pair than in P.
Order: R > Q > P.

questions.text:
A dipeptide, "x" on complete hydrolysis gives "y" and "z". "y" on treatment with aq. $\mathrm{HNO_2}$ produces lactic acid. On the other hand "z" on heating gives the following cyclic molecule.
Based on the information given, the dipeptide X is :
questions.sol:
Nitrous acid converts $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ to $\mathrm{-OH}$; lactic acid $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)COOH}$ comes from alanine $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH}$, so y is alanine.
The cyclic product is the diketopiperazine of glycine (two $\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups in the ring), so z is glycine.
The dipeptide is alanine-glycine.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$x$ mg of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}$ (molar mass = 58) is required to be dissolved in 1.0 L of water to produce a pH of 10.0 at 298 K. The value of $x$ is __________ mg. (Nearest integer)
(Given : $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}$ is assumed to dissociate completely in $\mathrm{H_2O}$]
questions.sol:
pH 10 means pOH 4, so $[\mathrm{OH^-}]=10^{-4}$ M.
$[\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}]=5\times10^{-5}$ M; mass in 1 L $=5\times10^{-5}\times58$ g $=2.9$ mg $\approx3$ mg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The molar conductance of an infinitely dilute solution of ammonium chloride was found to be 185 S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$ and the ionic conductance of hydroxyl and chloride ions are 170 and 70 S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, respectively. If molar conductance of 0.02 M solution of ammonium hydroxide is 85.5 S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, its degree of dissociation is given by $x\times10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is __________. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
By Kohlrausch's law, $\Lambda^\circ_m(\mathrm{NH_4OH})=\Lambda^\circ_m(\mathrm{NH_4Cl})+\lambda^\circ(\mathrm{OH^-})-\lambda^\circ(\mathrm{Cl^-})=185+170-70=285$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$.
$\alpha=\dfrac{85.5}{285}=0.3=3\times10^{-1}$, so $x=3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Sea water, which can be considered as a 6 molar (6 M) solution of NaCl, has a density of 2 g mL$^{-1}$. The concentration of dissolved oxygen $(\mathrm{O_2})$ in sea water is 5.8 ppm. Then the concentration of dissolved oxygen $(\mathrm{O_2})$ in sea water, is $x\times10^{-4}$ m.
$x=$__________. (Nearest integer)
Given : Molar mass of NaCl is 58.5 g mol$^{-1}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{O_2}$ is 32 g mol$^{-1}$
questions.sol:
Take 1 L of sea water: mass 2000 g, containing $6\times58.5=351$ g NaCl, so the water is $1649$ g.
$\mathrm{O_2}$: $5.8\times10^{-6}\times2000=0.0116$ g $=3.625\times10^{-4}$ mol.
Molality $=\dfrac{3.625\times10^{-4}}{1.649}\approx2.2\times10^{-4}$ m, so $x=2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The amount of calcium oxide produced on heating 150 kg limestone (75% pure) is __________ kg. (Nearest integer)
Given : Molar mass (in g mol$^{-1}$) of Ca-40, O-16, C-12
questions.sol:
Pure $\mathrm{CaCO_3}=0.75\times150=112.5$ kg.
$\mathrm{CaCO_3\rightarrow CaO+CO_2}$: 100 g gives 56 g.
CaO $=112.5\times\dfrac{56}{100}=63$ kg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A metal complex with a formula $\mathrm{MCl_4.3NH_3}$ is involved in $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation. It upon reaction with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution gives 'x' moles of AgCl. Consider 'x' is equal to the number of lone pairs of electron present in central atom of $\mathrm{BrF_5}$. Then the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by the complex is __________.
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{BrF_5}$, Br has 7 valence electrons: 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, so x $=1$.
One ionisable chloride and six-coordination ($sp^3d^2$) give $\mathrm{[MCl_3(NH_3)_3]Cl}$.
An $\mathrm{MA_3B_3}$ octahedral complex has 2 geometrical isomers (fac and mer).
questions.subject: Chemistry
